localFacts.fact: Lufthansa allows a cabin bag of max. 55 x 40 x 23 cm; the Summit Carbon II (46 cm), Alpine CF-425 (47 cm) and VEO 3GO (34 cm) fit by length, the Ridgeview (74 cm folded) does not and goes in checked baggage.
Destatis (Mikrozensus 2025): men in Germany are on average 1,79 m (179,1 cm) tall; of the five tripods only the Ridgeview at 187 cm is taller.
In German shops the Primos Trigger Stick Gen. 3 Tall is sold as a "Zielstock" (Dreibein) with a 61 to 157 cm range.
The German Vortex distributor lists the Summit Carbon II at 1133 g and 9,9 kg max. load, the Ridgeview Carbon at 187 cm.

localPainPoints.pain: Mountain hunters question carrying a tripod at all because every gram counts.
localPainPoints.fix: Pick by optic: the Alpine CF-425 (907 g) or Summit Carbon II (1,13 kg) for seated glassing; for a quick look, rest the scope on the pack, and hang the pack from the hook in wind.

quotes.text: wozu willst du bei der Bergjagd noch ein zusätzliches Teil mitschleppen, da zählt doch das Gewicht?

localPainPoints.pain: A Bergstock (alpine staff) is tall enough but too wobbly as a rifle rest; hunters want a combined glassing tripod and rifle rest.
localPainPoints.fix: The Primos Trigger Stick Gen3 is a rifle rest first (61 to 157 cm, one hand) and its yoke swaps for an optics mount; glassing tripods like the Alpine are not made for a rifle.

quotes.text: Bergstock ist hoch genug, doch als Zielstock mir persönlich zu wackelig.

localPainPoints.pain: A wobbly tripod ruins glassing with a spotting scope; an angled scope needs a lower, steadier tripod.
localPainPoints.fix: Pan head (Videoneiger) instead of a ball head, legs wide and low, thickest sections first; with an angled scope the shorter tripod is enough.

quotes.text: So ein Wackelstativ ist eine Pest und verleidet einem das ganze Beobachten.
